book_meta.work: short stories by Guy de Maupassant and Anton Chekhov
book_meta.author: Maupassant (d. 1893) and Chekhov (d. 1904)
book_meta.status: public domain — retold from the plots, not from any translation

sentences.ar: بيوم سوق، رجل عجوز شاف خيط عالأرض.
sentences.en: On a market day, an old man saw a piece of string on the ground.
He bent down, took it and tucked it in his pocket.
A man who disliked him saw him bending.
That same day, a wallet was lost in the market.

sentences.ar: الرجل اللي بيكرهه راح عالشرطة وحكى.
sentences.en: The man who disliked him went to the police and spoke.

sentences.ar: استدعوا العجوز، وهو طلّع الخيط من جيبه.
sentences.en: They summoned the old man, and he took the string from his pocket.
After days, the wallet came back and was found.

sentences.ar: بس الناس ضلوا يحكوا: هو دبرها.
sentences.en: But people went on saying: he arranged it.

sentences.ar: العجوز صار يشرح لكل واحد بيقابله.
sentences.en: The old man began explaining to everyone he met.

sentences.ar: كل ما يشرح أكتر، كل ما صدقوه أقل.
sentences.en: The more he explained, the less they believed him.

sentences.ar: مرض ومات وهو لسا بيقول: كان خيط.
sentences.en: He fell ill and died still saying: it was a piece of string.
